clue.text: Not quite free to give the result of the division

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can be rearranged at will

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone almost at liberty, hoping to hand over the answer to a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite free' reads as 'nearly at liberty', but NOT QUITE is the fodder and 'free' the signal, giving QUOTIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the figure obtained when one number is divided by another is called by this technical name.

clue.text: Bat that may be held in the hand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stick or cudgel used for striking

definitions.text: that may be held in the hand
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the four card suits, held in a player's hand at bridge

explanation.surface: A bat is something you grip in your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hand' is a hand of cards, not the palm gripping a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy stick for hitting shares the name with a playing-card suit dealt to players at the table.

clue.text: A new bride's bits and pieces

indicators.note: a new version of something is made over, so the letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: the word taken letter for letter, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A newly married woman's odds and ends, as if listing her trousseau.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered fragments and leftover rubbish are collectively known by this word for broken remains.

clue.text: Turn, or intend to turn, Communist

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend to

indicators.note: to turn a word is to spin it round so it reads the other way

parts.note: Red is the standard nickname for a Communist

explanation.surface: A politician wavering, either changing sides or planning to defect to the Communists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' appears twice: the capitalised first one is the definition, the second is the signal acting on the Communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A river or path that bends and winds back and forth is said to wander in loops this way.

clue.text: Man's man, for instance

parts.note: surface reading: a manly fellow, the kind of man other men admire
setter's reading: Man is the Isle of Man, so its man is one of its inhabitants

explanation.walkthrough: The capital M is the giveaway: Man is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, so a Manx man is an ISLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Any resident of an island surrounded by sea, such as the Isle of Man, is called this.

clue.text: Time of occupation

parts.note: surface reading: a period when a country was held by foreign troops
setter's reading: occupation as one's job, so the time spent at work

explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' suggests a military one, but here it is employment: a WORKING DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily hours given to one's job, as opposed to weekends or holidays, form this period.

clue.text: Irishman at church for spiritual guidance

definitions.note: loose: the answer is a meeting held to seek guidance from spirits

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman goes to church to seek help for his soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a priest; the spirits wanted are those of the dead, contacted by a medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Participants at a sitting with a medium try to contact departed spirits, hoping for messages from beyond.

clue.text: A light gold

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lantern with a thick bulging lens, once used by police
second meaning: the gold centre of an archery target

explanation.walkthrough: 'A light gold' reads as a pale shade of gold; split it into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern with a convex glass lens bears the same name as the golden central ring of a target.

clue.text: Accounts to be settled in large numbers

explanation.surface: Many debts waiting to be paid off in bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Grudges awaiting revenge and great quantities (a score being twenty) share this plural word.

clue.text: Mad to reverse, try going forward

indicators.note: reversing a word makes its letters run from right to left

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Instructions for driving: it is crazy to back up, so attempt to move ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going forward' plays against 'reverse' for the surface; to have a stab at something is to attempt it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to make an attempt, so the noun means an attempt.

clue.text: Wasted no time collecting the loot?

definitions.text: Wasted no time collecting the loot?

parts.note: someone who wasted no time ran, hurrying
sacking a town means plundering it for loot

explanation.surface: A burglar hurrying to bag the stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition, with the question mark flagging the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Going through a place hastily and roughly to steal valuables is what thieves do when plundering.

clue.text: Feels one would be mad to be out of them

definitions.meaning: first meaning: perceives, becomes aware of

definitions.text: one would be mad to be out of them
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone out of their wits is said to be out of these

explanation.surface: A wry remark that losing one's grip would be madness.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive is to sense something, and a person gone crazy is idiomatically said to have taken leave of these faculties.

clue.text: Cliché of a hi-fi buff

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fixed, oversimplified image or idea
second meaning, split as two words

explanation.surface: The predictable image of a sound-system enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into STEREO TYPE for the hi-fi enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackneyed, conventional idea of a group is called this, and the word divides into a kind of audio fan.

clue.text: To put one at risk on purpose is a sin

definitions.note: infinitive phrase; the answer is the bare verb

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose, as in 'to that end'
anger, or wrath, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A moral pronouncement that deliberately exposing someone to harm is sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On purpose' reads as 'deliberately', but it supplies END, a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose a person or thing to harm or peril is to imperil them.

clue.text: Not a professor of divinity, evidently

definitions.text: Not a professor of divinity, evidently

parts.note: surface reading: someone who holds no university chair in theology
setter's reading: one who professes a belief, here a belief in God

explanation.walkthrough: A professor is also one who professes; someone who professes no belief in God is an ATHEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who denies the existence of any deity does not profess religious faith.

clue.text: Shortage of transport in southern metropolis

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a car is a means of transport
a metropolis is a large city

explanation.surface: Not enough buses and trains in a big city in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts transport inside the city, but the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack or insufficiency of something in demand is the state of being scarce.

clue.text: Boring commercial breaks into fight

definitions.note: adjective in the surface; the answer is a noun, a boring tool

indicators.note: something that breaks into a place forces its way inside it

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight
an ad is a commercial, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A dull advert interrupting a boxing match on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like 'dull', but it means 'tool for making holes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed hand tool used for making holes in wood before driving screws.

clue.text: Betting, using a pay-phone

parts.note: a wage is pay for work
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Placing bets by calling a bookmaker from a coin-operated telephone box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay-phone' is one thing in the surface but two pieces in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Staking money on an uncertain outcome is gambling, which is placing a wager.

clue.text: Singular-looking giant?

parts.note: surface reading: strange or odd in appearance
setter's reading: looking with a single eye, like the one-eyed giant of Greek myth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' means odd, but here it means 'one': the giant with a single eye.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these one-eyed giants included Polyphemus, whom Odysseus blinded.

clue.text: It rarely turns out like this in books

definitions.note: adjective phrase meaning bookish, of written works

indicators.note: something that turns out differently is altered, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A wry remark that real life seldom unfolds the way it does in novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Language or matters relating to written literature, as found in books, are described this way.

clue.text: Emphatic type

parts.note: surface reading: a forceful, assertive kind of person
setter's reading: type as printing letters, the sloping kind used for emphasis

explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' suggests a kind of person, but it is a printer's typeface, slanted for stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping printed lettering is used to stress words in a sentence, so it is a typeface of emphasis.

clue.text: Passage for half the convoy takes time

indicators.note: taking half of a word means dropping the other half of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Half of a group of ships needs a long time for a crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: It is the second half of the convoy that is kept, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey by sea is a passage, the usual word for a long sea trip.

clue.text: Starting with Virgo, Zodiac sign alters

indicators.note: the starting part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Virgo
Aries, the Ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An astrological remark that one star sign changes when Virgo begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgo sounds like the sign wanted; it only supplies its first letter, and the sign is ARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that changes or differs from time to time is said to fluctuate in this way.

clue.text: Fussy individual

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hard to please, choosy
second meaning: specific, single, as in this one case

explanation.surface: A finicky person.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an adjective describing a noun, but both words are adjectives.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both exacting in standards and relating to one specific item rather than many.

clue.text: Excellent yet not well done

definitions.meaning: second meaning: of meat, lightly cooked

explanation.surface: Praise for something that was nonetheless poorly executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not well done' sounds like a criticism; it describes a steak cooked lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptionally good, and of meat, cooked only briefly so the inside stays red.

clue.text: Adjourned for some wine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a meeting ... when it ended its session
second meaning: pink wine, written with an accent in French

explanation.surface: A meeting broke up so everyone could go for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A court or parliament stood up at the close of business, and a pink wine bears the same name.

clue.text: Payment to a girlfriend is a fur cape

parts.note: a tip is a small extra payment for service
pet is an affectionate name for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A gift given to a girlfriend turns out to be a fur wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A short shoulder cape, often of fur, worn by women or as part of academic or clerical dress.

clue.text: Delightful lake in rustic surroundings

indicators.note: something put in a place is set inside it
surroundings enclose whatever sits within them

parts.note: a rustic is a country dweller, a peasant
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A charming lake set in pretty countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustic' looks like an adjective describing the scenery, but it is the noun for a country person.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable and pleasing to be with or look at, giving enjoyment.
